title: Compound angles
goal: I can expand and use compound angle formulas.
teach: sin(α ± β) = sin α cos β ± cos α sin β; cos(α ± β) = cos α cos β ∓ sin α sin β (note the sign swap for cos). Use them to find exact values such as sin 75° = sin(45° + 30°), and to recognise expansions in reverse.
tvis:
FormulaExample
sin(α + β)sin 75° = sin 45° cos 30° + cos 45° sin 30°
cos(α − β)cos 70° cos 10° + sin 70° sin 10° = cos 60°

steps: = √22 × √32 + √22 × ½.

watch:
sin(A + B) is not sin A + sin B.

Problem-solving lens
Look for the pattern sin cos + cos sin, or cos cos ∓ sin sin, and fold it back into one angle.

qs.text: sin A = 35 and cos B = 513, with A and B acute. Find sin(A + B).
qs.hint: cos A = 45, sin B = 1213
qs.steps:
1. Formulas (point P(x; y) on the terminal arm): r = √(x² + y²) (always positive); sin θ = yr; cos θ = xr; tan θ = yx.
2. sin A = 35: cos A = 45 (3-4-5 triangle). cos B = 513: sin B = 1213 (5-12-13 triangle)
3. Formulas (compound angles): sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B; cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B.
4. sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B = 35513 + 451213
5. = 1565 + 4865 = 6365
